summary: The geometric area computations and the exclusion of a middle triangle with normalized area ratio 1/100:1:1 are correct, but the claimed matrix infeasibility does not follow from the supplied predecessor facts by the argument given.
critical_errors: The proof asserts that every transformed strict matrix system has the exact area ratio 1/100:1:1 and hence B=1. Accepted fact 09393c6edf1fc4e2 gives only |P0|:|P1|:|P2|=A:1:B. Fixing P0 and P2 and their ratio 1/100 determines A/B=1/100, not B=1 or |P1|=|P2|. Thus equations (6)-(7) exclude only B=1 and do not exclude completions with B different from 1.
gaps: No argument is supplied to rule out the allowed B different from 1 values from the strict residual strip, so the Consequence statement and the claims about arbitrary cap and sign-cell data are unproved.

The final assertion about middle coordinate caps and sign-cell areas and neighborhoods of the displayed four-tuple does not define those quantities in the candidate or supplied predecessors, so its exact content cannot be checked.
repair_hints: For a putative completion, combine |P0|/|P2|=A/B=1/100 with the reduced q=2 branch to get R=1/100 and S=1/B. The residual strip then gives 99/100<1/B<101/100, whereas Q contained in P1 gives B=|P2|/|P1|<=1/42. These inequalities are incompatible. State this argument explicitly instead of setting B=1.
Define the cap and sign-cell quantities and the topology underlying every neighborhood, or omit that imprecise add-on.
